newsitem.title: MEXICO: TV Azteca extends debt exchange offer.
newsitem.headline: TV Azteca extends debt exchange offer.

text.p: Mexico's second-largest broadcaster TV Azteca said on Monday it was extending by a month its offer to swap outstanding A and B series debt for similar paper registered under the Securities Act of 1933.

In a statement released in Mexico City late on Monday, the newly floated media firm said it was extending by 30 calendar days its offer to exchange 10-1/8 percent series A Guaranteed Senior Notes due in 2004, and 10-1/2 series B Guaranteed Senior Notes due 2007, for paper of the same rate and maturity that had been registered under the 1933 Securities Act.
TV Azteca said the current exchange offers, scheduled to expire at 1700 local time on August 18, 1997, would now expire at 1700 local time on September 17.
The extended exchange offers would still remain subject to the terms and conditions of the current exchange offers, the statement said.

TV Azteca dazzled Mexican investors last week when it went public with the largest initial offering of Mexican stock since the 1994 peso crisis. It sold 18.5 percent of the company for a total of $526 million in a global offering in Mexico, the United States and Europe.
